title: No roofs, no toilets, no teachers: TOI check finds minuses in Rajasthan govt schools
content: TOI reporters visited govt schools in 6 Rajasthan districts after the CJP row. The findings show how basic govt schooling has collapsed in pockets of the state, from the coaching capital of Kota to desert villages and Jhalawar’s tragedy-hit Piplodi.

title: 'Umpires' calls & different ball': Root explains lean run as he chases Sachin’s record
content: Joe Root remains confident despite a difficult batting summer for England. He believes challenging conditions and the Dukes ball have impacted all batters. Root has scored only twice over fifty this season, averaging 29.44. He is still focused on surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's Test run record. England secured a series win against Pakistan under his captaincy.

title: Oracle layoffs: Company leadership may again send the '6 am' email on September 1
content: Oracle employees expect layoff emails on September 1, the day its fiscal second quarter begins, with managers asked to submit lists of affected employees and some teams facing double-digit cuts. Staff fear a repeat of March 31, when a 6 am email from "Oracle Leadership" told 10,000 workers their role was eliminated. Oracle has already cut 21,000 jobs this fiscal year while spending $55.7 billion on AI data centres.

title: US Open: Mariano Navone wins battle as Novak Djokovic’s body says no
content: Mariano Navone pulled off an incredible upset by defeating Novak Djokovic in a hard-fought five-set match. Despite dealing with health issues and requiring medical aid, Djokovic showcased his legendary tenacity, coming back from two sets down. However, Navone executed his tactics flawlessly and remained focused, marking a career-defining victory against one of the sport's greatest players.

title: Stranger ran past Nepal school screaming ‘run, water’. It saved 370 kids, teachers
content: An unidentified man's warning saved over 370 pupils and teachers from a massive flood. Students and staff scrambled to a forested hill as floodwaters surged rapidly. Communications were disrupted, making it difficult to account for all students after the event. One father tragically perished while attempting to reach the school for his son. The school continues efforts to trace pupils and reunite them with their families.

title: From exam reforms to school reforms: How CJP is changing political discourse
content: Student protests for improved school conditions have shifted from cities to villages across India.  The Cockroach Janata Party's campaign exposed poor government school infrastructure in several states.  State governments responded with new regulations and accelerated development projects.  Political parties are now focusing on youth outreach and educational issues.  This movement highlights youth as potential game-changers in electoral politics.

title: Starting September 1, Indian airports are discontinuing immigration clearance
content: From September 1, international travellers at Indian airports will experience a streamlined process for immigration clearance. The need for stamped boarding passes will be eliminated, allowing passengers to present either digital or printed passes. This change is designed to enhance efficiency and reduce wait times, as immigration officers will no longer stamp boarding passes during the departure process.

title: India’s GPS problem: Why the armed forces need NavIC to work
content: India's NavIC satellite system, crucial for military and civilian use, currently has only three operational satellites. This shortfall impacts its ability to provide accurate positioning and navigation services. The system's reliability issues stemmed from imported atomic clocks, now being replaced by indigenous ones. Upcoming launches aim to restore the full constellation's functionality. This indigenous capability is vital for India's strategic autonomy and modernization efforts.

title: Microsoft admits AI is making it tough to meet ‘environmental commitments’
content: Microsoft is taking significant steps to alleviate employee worries regarding the ecological footprint of its data centers. As the demand for artificial intelligence intensifies, the firm grapples with its promises to cut greenhouse gas emissions. In response to public criticism and local resistance, Microsoft is prioritizing innovative engineering and efficiency improvements, while also refining its approaches to renewable energy and carbon management.

title: ‘Everyone is worried’: Pakistan languish at WTC bottom after another heavy defeat
content: Pakistan's Test team faces deep concerns after another heavy away defeat.  Pacer Mohammad Abbas admitted that everyone is worried about the team's current performances.  Dropped catches at Lord's allowed England to score significantly more runs.  The team's batting, bowling, and fielding are all areas needing improvement.  Pakistan's young pace attack is still adjusting to Test cricket demands.

title: Italy population to shrink by nearly 4 million by 2050 as ageing accelerates
content: Italy's population is projected to significantly decrease by 2050.  Birth rates remain low, while the elderly population is expected to grow.  This demographic shift will create new economic and welfare system challenges.  Southern regions anticipate the most substantial population losses across the country.  Immigration has previously helped stabilize the population figures.

title: Manchester United fans baffled as Old Trafford roof still leaks
content: Manchester United's Old Trafford stadium roof leaked heavily during a recent match. Water poured through the roof, creating a waterfall effect for fans. This recurring issue has frustrated supporters and raised stadium condition concerns. The club has invested significantly in new players this summer. However, the stadium's infrastructure problems continue to be a major talking point.

title: Faf revisits cricket’s darkest chapter, says Australia mishandled ‘Sandpaper Gate’
content: Faf du Plessis has voiced his views regarding the media's portrayal of Cameron Bancroft, suggesting it was unduly severe. The former South African captain empathizes with the Australian batsman and critiques Cricket Australia's management of the situation along with outside influences. Du Plessis proposes that financial repercussions would have sufficed, arguing that the imposed bans are excessive in relation to Bancroft's actions.

title: ‘Social media player’: Ex-Pakistan cricketer brutally tears into Babar Azam
content: Former Pakistan batter Basit Ali strongly criticized captain Babar Azam following another batting failure.  Azam's recent Test performances and lack of centuries drew significant criticism from Ali.  Ali questioned Azam's contribution during difficult match situations for the team.  Other Pakistan batters, including Saud Shakeel and Mohammad Rizwan, also faced Ali's sharp critique.  Pakistan suffered a significant defeat in the second Test against England, losing the series.

title: 8 dead, several injured in blast at cracker manufacturing unit in UP
content: A massive explosion ripped through a firecracker unit on Monday.  At least eleven people died and five others sustained injuries in the blast.  The incident occurred in the Pipri police station area near Manori power house.  Rescue operations were launched by police and fire brigade personnel.  The blast also damaged several nearby houses and shattered windows.

title: From watching Djokovic win 1st Slam to sending his idol home: Mariano Navone's story
content: Mariano Navone stunned childhood idol Novak Djokovic in a dramatic five-set US Open opener, earning the biggest win of his career. The 25-year-old Argentine’s journey began at a local club aged three before five Challenger titles helped shape his rise. Known as “La Navoneta”, Navone’s dream became reality as he beat the player he once called “very special”.

title: Tamim hopeful on India series, admits B'desh ‘could have dealt’ with T20 WC better
content: Tamim Iqbal, the president of Bangladesh Cricket Board, expresses optimism about arranging a white-ball series against India. He acknowledges that the earlier management regarding the withdrawal from the 2026 T20 World Cup could have been more prudent. Both cricket boards are diligently searching for an appropriate time for this tour.

title: What’s forced Russia to import 1 million barrels in 2 months from India
content: Russia’s seaborne gasoline imports climbed to a record level of around 125,000 barrels per day (kbd) in August, which would amount to about 470,000 tonnes for the month. Reports suggest that Indian refiners supplied as much as 1 million barrels of gasoline to Russia over the past two months.

title: 'Women should stay confined to homes': Kerala Islamic scholar Kanthapuram
content: Islamic scholar Kanthapuram A P Aboobacker Musliyar stated women should remain confined to their homes. He defended a recent circular from his organization which advised women against public platforms. Musliyar cited religious texts which he believes mandate purdah for women's protection. He asserted that knowledgeable scholars have taught these views for a century. The scholar vowed to continue expressing these opinions despite criticism.

title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, breaks all-time Duleep Trophy record
content: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set a new Duleep Trophy record as the youngest batter to score a half-century. He achieved this milestone at fifteen years and 175 days old during the semi-final match. Sooryavanshi narrowly missed a century, finishing with an impressive ninety-two runs off eighty-one balls. He also briefly captained East Zone after Ishan Kishan's injury. Central Zone was bowled out for 266 earlier in the day.

title: No internet needed: PhonePe brings UPI payments to over 200m feature phone users
content: PhonePe has launched UPI 123Pay, enabling feature phone users to transact digitally. This service extends UPI payment capabilities to over two hundred million Indian feature phone users.  The platform allows peer-to-peer and peer-to-merchant payments, and balance checks.  It also offers an AI-powered helpline for first-time users in multiple languages.  Future updates will introduce utility bill payments and mobile recharges.

title: India GDP growth defies US-Iran war impact, economy grows at robust 7.8% in Q1
content: The latest growth figure was also higher than the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) earlier projection of 7 per cent for Q1 FY27. The central bank had estimated quarterly growth at 7 per cent earlier this month, while raising its full-year FY27 growth forecast to 6.7 per cent from 6.6 per cent.

title: Centre moves Supreme Court to quash FIRs against NEET protesters
content: The Centre has asked the Supreme Court to quash FIRs against NEET protesters.  Solicitor General Tushar Mehta presented this plea before the Chief Justice.  The Supreme Court will hear this significant matter on September 1.  Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janta Party announced a new protest march.  This march will occur in Delhi on September 5 over unfulfilled assurances.

title: Tensions escalate in Manipur as 2 villagers killed, another injured in gun attack
content: Two villagers were killed and another injured in a gun attack by suspected militants. Armed men opened indiscriminate fire at N Teikhang village, killing two persons and burning houses. The firing forced several villagers to flee their homes and seek shelter in nearby forests. A heavy exchange of fire was underway between armed groups belonging to two communities.

title: From garbage mountains to cleaner cities: How Delhi is showing India the way
content: Delhi's innovative approach to environmental management has resulted in the reclamation of 100 acres by converting legacy waste from landfills into usable land. This remarkable step not only mitigates previous waste challenges but also highlights the need for ongoing daily waste management to prevent the formation of new refuse piles.

title: Sukesh Chandrasekhar sentenced to 8-year jail term for impersonating SC judge
content: A Delhi court has sentenced Sukesh Chandrasekhar to eight years rigorous imprisonment. He impersonated a Supreme Court judge to influence a bail proceeding. The court imposed fines and consecutive sentences for his criminal actions. Chandrasekhar's unsuccessful attempt did not mitigate his severe sentence. This ruling sends a strong deterrent message to protect the justice system.

title: Man stabs friend to death for eating more chicken pieces during drunken brawl
content: A man allegedly stabbed his friend to death during a drunken brawl over chicken. The deceased was identified as Sathiram Chandradev, a native of Uttar Pradesh. The accused, Arunkumar Balishtar Chavan, is from the same village and worked at a steel factory. Arunkumar accused Sathiram of taking more chicken and stabbed him with a nearby knife. Police cracked the case and arrested Arunkumar, seizing the murder weapon.

title: Nepal floods: Boy waves T-shirt for help, climbs onto helicopter in dramatic rescue
content: A dramatic rescue unfolded as a Nepal Army helicopter lifted a young boy from a rooftop inundated by floodwaters. The boy's signal, a T-shirt waving for help, drew the attention of the helicopter crew, showcasing bravery amidst ongoing flood relief operations. Tragically, the region is grappling with severe loss, with reports of hundreds dead and thousands unaccounted for as diligent rescue efforts carry on.

title: Heavy rain, darkness, drawn curtains: The bus ride that ended in gang rape
content: A shocking incident unfolded as a 16-year-old girl was gang-raped aboard a moving sleeper bus en route to Kashmere Gate. The bus driver and conductor are accused of committing this horrific act before abandoning the traumatized student 47 kilometers later. Police swiftly apprehended the suspects in a nearby bus parking area, while the vehicle was sent for forensic analysis following the harrowing event.

title: AIMIM party worker killed 100 metres from his house in Hyderabad
content: An AIMIM party worker was fatally stabbed by a group near his home. The victim, Md Mahboob Ali, was attacked while returning from a local hotel. Six assailants on two motorcycles inflicted multiple stab wounds before fleeing the scene. Local leaders visited the site and confirmed the victim's party affiliation. Police have identified a prime suspect and are actively pursuing the accused.

title: 16-year-old girl gang-raped inside moving bus during 47-km ride to Delhi
content: A 16-year-old student was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus. She had boarded the vehicle seeking help while stranded in heavy rain. The driver and conductor then allegedly raped her and threatened her life. They abandoned the terrified teenager near Kashmere Gate bus terminal. Police arrested the accused and seized the bus for examination.

title: Big four-tracking push! Railways to expand on 7 high-density routes - why it matters
content: India’s seven high-density railway routes, covering about 11,000 km, are being expanded to four tracks to handle more passenger and freight traffic across the country, Vaishnaw said recently.

Additionally, he expressed reservations regarding the Dukes cricket ball used this summer, pondering its impact on the pitches.

title: Delhi gangrape on moving bus: DCW chairperson says culprits ‘must get punishment’
content: women commission chairperson lata Gupta condemns the gangrape of a 16-year-old girl inside a sleeper bus . police have subsequently arrested Kuldeep and Sandeep from a bus parking area in Timarpur . the girl boarded the bus seeking help amid heavy rain, police say .

title: Nepal floods revive Bihar’s annual nightmare: Why the state faces flooding every year
content: the rivers that sustain the region for most of the year turn dangerous during the monsoon . the flooding has long been a part of life in northern Bihar . a growing population and rapid urbanisation have made their impact more severe over the years .

title: 'Venezuela will be reborn': Maduro shares first photos from US prison since capture
content: Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, will "remain strong, serene, and confident" the 63-year-old smiles and flashes a peace sign in a photograph . the photos were released on august 30, timestamps indicate they were taken on June 25 .

title: Watch: Zohran Mamdani look-alike contest draws hundreds in New York
content: dozens gathered near Washington Square Park on Sunday for a look-alike contest . drew on different phases of the mayor's public life, from politics and basketball to cycling . comedian and actor Amadeo Fusca won the $100 prize in a new york Knicks jersey paired with formalwear .

title: Rahul or Vijay for PM? Congress-TVK rift talk grows after MLA’s seat shift
content: state tourism minister says government ministers would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as prime ministerial candidate for 2029 Lok Sabha elections . the remarks come amid statements by TVK leaders projecting party chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as a potential contender for the PM's post .

title: Nepal flash floods: Death toll rises to 903, over 4,200 still missing
content: the death toll from catastrophic flash floods and landslides in Nepal has risen to 903 . the disaster has also left 4,247 people missing, while 10,451 people have been rescued so far . nearly 20,000 security personnel and 14 military helicopters have been deployed for rescue and relief operations .

title: Meet the 19-year-old who built a $600,000 investment house from scratch
content: Olivia Shone started saving for property at age 16 after discussions with her father . she bought a plot of land in her hometown and built a house on it three years later . the total investment was estimated at about $600,000 .

title: Oregon farmer grows crops for 40 years without irrigation
content: dry farming is a technique for growing crops without irrigation by carefully managing the moisture already in the soil . he started dry farming in California but moved to a 9.6-acre site near Veneta, Oregon, in 2007 . over decades, weather patterns became less predictable across the Pacific Northwest .

title: 'No jurisdiction, illegal': India tears into Hague court's Indus Waters Treaty award
content: new Delhi's decision to put the water treaty with Pakistan in abeyance "will remain in force," MEA says . the ministry categorically rejects the ruling, calling it an "illegally constituted" organisation . "this so-called Court was constituted by the world bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty," the ministry said .

title: PM Modi's jackets, Rahul's shirts: How leaders use fashion for political messaging
content: a politician's clothes have helped construct identities, signal ideology, project modernity, invoke tradition and increasingly generate the kind of visual moments that social media loves . when Rahul Gandhi appeared in a pink shirt, the change from his usual white clothing drew attention online .
